title: Majestic Domination
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to win with only a bishop and a knight left against an entire queen. But white knows that it is all a matter of a coordination of pieces. And so he starts with bishop to c5 check. A beautiful little sacrifice that cannot be accepted or this would be a fork attacking the king and queen and winning the game. These squares are defended by the knight and going here would still allow a fork. So the king [music] only has one option, going to a5. Now white really has to tread carefully and continue to attack the black king. So knight to c6 forces king to a4. There doesn't seem to be another way to check this black king. But white finds the very cool, calm and collected king to a2. Now setting up a checkmate threat. If black is careless now and for example picks up this pawn, pawn to b3 would be a checkmate in one. So black cannot allow that and the only [music] way to prevent the checkmate is to play pawn to b4 opening up an escape square for the king. Now of course there is no checkmate anymore. But white still plays the mysterious b3 check. And this seems to be a blunder because after king to b5, now the bishop and the knight are forked by the king and he is going to pick up one of the two on the next move. So is this it? Has white messed up and is going to lose the game? Well, not exactly. Knight to d4 check. Remembering that the king can actually not take the bishop because of this fork. So instead the king is forced back to a5. Now coming back with the knight would at least secure a draw by repetition. But white wants more than a draw and so he plays the third brilliant sacrifice with bishop takes e7. This gives up the bishop, but again of course the bishop cannot be taken because of a fork. And not only that, if you move the queen away, this is a checkmate in just two moves. But at the last, this is not a problem because the black queen can just stay defending the d8 square, and now there is no more checks and no more threats. Except that there is. Because queen h8 does not stop bishop to d8 check. This is almost checkmate. So, the bishop has to be captured. But you guessed it. We have placed the king and the queen in the perfect position to deliver a knight fork, and white is going to pick up the queen and win the game. Follow me if you love incredible chess.
